\[
\left|\frac{f(t)-f(x)}{t-x}\right|\le |t-x|.
\]
As $t\to x$, the right-hand side tends to $0$, so
\[
\lim_{t\to x}\frac{f(t)-f(x)}{t-x}=0.
\]
Thus $f$ is differentiable at every $x\in\mathbb R$ and $f'(x)=0$ for all $x$. By the mean value theorem, for any $a<b$ there exists $c\in(a,b)$ such that
\[
f(b)-f(a)=f'(c)(b-a)=0.
\]
Hence $f(a)=f(b)$ for all $a,b\in\mathbb R$, so $f$ is constant.
\end{proof}

\[
x_k=a+\frac{k}{n}(b-a),\qquad k=0,1,\dots,n.
\]
By the triangle inequality and the hypothesis,
\[
|f(b)-f(a)|
\le \sum_{k=1}^n |f(x_k)-f(x_{k-1})|

\]

\begin{proof}
We prove directly that any two values of $f$ agree. Let $a,b\in\mathbb R$ and let $n\ge1$. Define
\[
x_k=a+\frac{k}{n}(b-a)\quad (k=0,1,\ldots,n).
\]
Then $x_0=a$, $x_n=b$, and $|x_k-x_{k-1}|=|b-a|/n$. Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
|f(b)-f(a)|
&\le \sum_{k=1}^n |f(x_k)-f(x_{k-1})|\\
&\le \sum_{k=1}^n |x_k-x_{k-1}|^2\\
&=n\left(\frac{|b-a|}{n}\right)^2
=\frac{|b-a|^2}{n}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Because this bound holds for every $n$, letting $n\to\infty$ yields $|f(b)-f(a)|=0$. Thus $f(b)=f(a)$. Since $a$ and $b$ are arbitrary, $f$ is constant.
\end{proof}
